The defence has conceded 145 points across the three games, leaving them with a tournament point difference of -96. Their last outing in the third round ended in a 17-33 defeat against Scotland.

teams.heading: Emmanuel Iyogun embraces front-row conversion after making his senior England debut
teams.body: Northampton prop Emmanuel Iyogun has opened up about his transition from a reluctant teenage number eight to England's newest front-row option. After making his senior international debut off the bench against Argentina in July, the Spain-born forward admitted his early scrummaging experiences were far from smooth. Initially teased by teammates for running away from rucks, Iyogun persevered to earn Steve Borthwick's trust, demonstrating the raw resilience that has defined his unlikely rise to the senior Test squad.

teams.heading: Peter O'Mahony admits Rassie Erasmus's Munster departure 'hurt' him deeply
teams.body: Ireland legend Peter O'Mahony has opened up about the emotional toll of Rassie Erasmus's departure from Munster in 2017. Speaking on the Indo Sport podcast to promote his new book, All In, the veteran flanker confessed he felt personally aggrieved when the director of rugby returned to South Africa. "I was hurt because I trusted him and I was all into his game plan, and I was driving that for him," O'Mahony revealed. Despite the initial sting, he conceded the move made business sense.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham sidelined until next year as Josh McKay nears Scotland call
teams.body: Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham will remain unavailable until the end of the year after suffering a ruptured bicep. Head coach Sean Everitt described the injury as freakish, with the blow ruling the finisher out of the November test series. Consequently, Glasgow Warriors full-back Josh McKay is being tipped for a potential debut. McKay has been a consistent performer since 2021 and is now eligible to provide depth behind Blair Kinghorn and Kyle Rowe in the Nations Championship.

lead.why: It reports a significant injury to a key Scotland international and the emergence of a potential new cap for the November window.

teams.heading: Josh Adams confirms fitness for November tests while targeting third World Cup
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams expects to be fit for the upcoming Nations Championship fixtures after missing the summer tour of South Africa with a calf injury. The 31-year-old, who has 72 caps, has returned to training with Cardiff and anticipates a club comeback later this month. With one year until the 2027 World Cup opener against Zimbabwe in Adelaide, Adams is determined to secure a spot in Australia, stating: "I'm desperate to go, but there is loads of rugby to be played."

lead.why: Josh Adams provides a definitive fitness update for the upcoming November tests and outlines his long-term international ambitions for the next World Cup.

teams.heading: Hunter Paisami misses All Blacks Tests as Bledisloe Cup appeal fails
teams.body: Wallabies centre Hunter Paisami will miss the upcoming Bledisloe Cup series against New Zealand after failing to overturn a four-week suspension. The 28-year-old appealed an initial six-match ban for a dangerous tackle on South Africa’s Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu during the 42-38 victory in Perth. While the SANZAAR committee applied a two-week reduction for his remorse and conduct, the final sanction excludes him from the Tests in Auckland and Sydney. Les Kiss has called up Queensland Reds full-back Jock Campbell to replace the midfielder.

lead.why: The definitive failure of Hunter Paisami's suspension appeal and the subsequent naming of Jock Campbell as his replacement is the most significant squad development.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea confirms long-awaited move to Blues for 2027 Super Rugby season
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has confirmed his return to New Zealand rugby, signing with the Blues for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season. The 32-year-old loose forward joins the Auckland-based franchise following a stint in Japan with the Kobe Steelers under current national coach Dave Rennie. Savea, who previously represented the now-defunct Moana Pasifika, cited a desire to unite the city’s diverse cultures as a primary motivation. Blues chief executive Karl Budge praised Savea’s leadership, noting he will make a "huge contribution" both on and off the field.

lead.why: Ardie Savea is the national captain and his return to New Zealand domestic rugby is a major career milestone.

Reflecting on their time together, O’Mahony admitted he was "hurt" when the current SA Rugby director of rugby left for his national role, noting, "I trusted him and I was all into his game plan." O’Mahony, who described Erasmus as "good mad," acknowledged that despite the pain of his departure, Erasmus’s subsequent success confirmed his high coaching quality.
